meta.title: Why AI. Why now.
meta.dataNote: Adapted from Why AI, Why Now - Executive Keynote Ideas. Figures and links are transcribed from the supplied deck, not independently reverified. Forecasts, survey populations and study outcomes are distinguished.

scenes.title: Why AI.|Why now.
scenes.description: The technology is moving. The real question is how we turn possibility into value.
notes: Open with a leadership question, not a product demo: what would we redesign if intelligence were no longer the scarce resource?
This adaptation preserves the source deck's 16 ideas and six-act structure. Data is as supplied in the October 2026 deck, not independently verified.
scenes.takeaway: Move from using AI to redesigning work.

scenes.title: Six acts.|One leadership choice.
scenes.description: Follow the whole argument, or select an act to jump into the conversation.
notes: The first two acts explain why this wave is different and why timing matters. The middle acts separate usage from value and productivity from growth.
The final acts turn the frontier-firm idea into an operating model, then focus leadership on skills, data and governance.
scenes.takeaway: Capability creates possibility. Organization turns it into value.

scenes.title: From a few minutes|to a meaningful workflow.
scenes.description: The benchmark task horizon is stretching. The unit of ambition can stretch with it.
scenes.insight: Ask which multi-step outcome is becoming feasible, not which isolated task can be automated.
scenes.caveat: 50% benchmark success is not reliable production autonomy. Milestones are evenly spaced categories, not a time axis.
notes: The chart shows the duration of tasks a model can complete at a 50% success threshold: 3.5, 60, 121, 214 and 320 minutes at the five stated milestones.

The deck reports an 89-day doubling time since 2024 versus roughly seven months historically. Its separate Terminal-Bench comparison, 20% to 77.3%, measures something different and is not placed on this axis.
Treat this as a signal to revisit workflow scope. Production systems still need evaluation, supervision, access controls and failure handling.
scenes.takeaway: Redesign workflows as capability improves; do not confuse a benchmark with a service-level guarantee.

scenes.title: When intelligence gets cheaper,|the opportunity set changes.
scenes.description: A GPT-3.5-level capability moved from a premium input toward a commodity input.

visual.annotation: Same capability threshold. Very different economics.

scenes.metricLabel: cheaper, as summarized in the source
scenes.insight: A use case that failed the business case yesterday may deserve another look today.
scenes.caveat: The stated dates span about 23 months. Inference price is not the total cost of an AI solution.
notes: The source compares $20 per million tokens in November 2022 with $0.07 in October 2024 at a GPT-3.5-level capability threshold.

The deck calls this roughly 280-fold cheaper. The values imply about 286-fold; the visual retains the source's approximate headline. Its '18 months' wording is not repeated because the stated dates span roughly 23 months.

The source also reports a 142-fold smaller model for the same MMLU level, hardware cost declining 30% annually and energy efficiency improving 40%. These are different measures, not extra reductions to multiply together.
scenes.takeaway: Recalculate economics, including integration, governance, evaluation and operating costs.

scenes.title: People did not wait|for the enterprise roadmap.
scenes.description: Early US adult adoption of generative AI outpaced these earlier technology comparisons.

visual.unit: US adults adopting / early adoption comparison

scenes.metricLabel: US adult GenAI adoption after two years
scenes.insight: Meet employees where they already are, with approved tools and a clear way to learn.
scenes.source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, Sep 2024
scenes.caveat: Different exposure periods: PC is at three years. This is not a global-population comparison.
notes: The relevant comparison is 39.4% for generative AI after two years, roughly 20% for the internet after two years, and roughly 20% for PCs after three years.

The source also mentions ChatGPT reaching 100 million users in two months, 900 million weekly users in February 2026 and a separate global adoption estimate. Those figures have different populations, periods and definitions and are not combined.
The leadership response is not to equate usage with value. It is to provide a safe route from individual experimentation to useful, measured work.
scenes.takeaway: Govern workforce adoption without suppressing useful experimentation.

scenes.title: Rent the frontier.|Own the differentiation.
scenes.description: The source's worldwide AI spending series signals a large infrastructure and market build-out.
scenes.insight: Use shared frontier infrastructure. Build advantage in your data, workflows, people and customer experience.
scenes.caveat: 2026 and 2027 are forecasts, not completed spending. Spending is not a measure of realized business value.
notes: The source series is $1.79 trillion in 2025, $2.67 trillion in 2026 and $3.64 trillion in 2027. Forecast years are outlined and explicitly marked F.
Separate source figures for corporate investment, $581.7 billion in 2025, and private investment, $344.7 billion, are different categories. They are not added to worldwide spending here.
The leadership question is where your organization should own differentiation rather than replicate a frontier infrastructure race.
scenes.takeaway: Rent scale; invest in the parts of the business that make you distinctive.

scenes.title: A regional head start|is not a permanent lead.
scenes.description: Nordic enterprise AI adoption is ahead of the EU benchmark. Now convert breadth into depth.
scenes.insight: How much of a valuable workflow has changed, not just how many firms have tried AI?
scenes.caveat: Enterprise adoption is not worker adoption, usage intensity or economic impact.
notes: The 2025 enterprise comparison is Denmark 42.0%, Finland 37.8%, Sweden 35.0% and the EU 20.0%. The denominator is enterprises with at least ten employees.
The deck's additional comparisons of US versus European worker adoption and output per hour use other populations and periods. They are not overlaid on this chart.
A 22-percentage-point adoption lead for Denmark is a useful starting position, not evidence that business transformation has already happened.
scenes.takeaway: Convert a regional adoption advantage into workflow intensity and measured value.

scenes.title: Usage is widespread.|Value is much less so.
scenes.description: Five survey signals reveal the distance between experimentation and enterprise performance.

visual.unit: Organization survey snapshots / not sequential conversion stages

scenes.insight: Name the P&L-relevant outcomes, redesign the work, and hold the transformation to a measurable result.
scenes.source: McKinsey State of AI, Aug 2026 / 1,719 respondents, 97 countries
scenes.caveat: Survey snapshots are not a measured funnel or a common cohort's conversion rate.
notes: The source reports roughly 90% regular use, 80% individual productivity improvement, 44% enterprise scaling, 37% some EBIT impact and around 6% high performers.
These percentages are shown as separate survey indicators. The graphic does not imply that one group progresses sequentially through all five stages.
The source also contrasts workflow redesign among high performers, about 75%, with about 25% among others. This association supports a redesign discussion, not a causal guarantee.
scenes.takeaway: Do not stop at adoption. Redesign three workflows with accountable economic outcomes.

scenes.title: The leaders are not just|using more technology.
scenes.description: BCG's future-built organizations outperform laggards across three different outcome measures.
scenes.metricLabel: source-reported leader time to impact, versus 17
scenes.insight: The performance story points toward people, processes and organization, not algorithms alone.
scenes.caveat: Different outcome metrics are not additive. Observational comparisons do not establish AI causation.
notes: BCG's comparison indexes laggards at 1.0. Future-built organizations show 2.3 times shareholder return, 2.4 times revenue growth and 2.8 times EBITDA growth.
These are separate performance comparisons, not a combined return and not proof that installing a tool causes the difference.
The source reports time to impact around eleven months for leaders versus seventeen for others. The next scene isolates the deck's 10/20/70 leadership heuristic.
scenes.takeaway: Build an operating-model advantage, not just a larger tool portfolio.

scenes.title: Fund the part|that changes the work.
scenes.description: A technology program becomes a business transformation when the organization changes with it.

visual.unit: BCG's transformation effort heuristic / not measured budget shares

scenes.insight: Assign ownership for redesigned work, not only ownership for deploying the technology.
scenes.caveat: 10/20/70 is a leadership heuristic, not a universal or empirically measured budget allocation.
notes: The deck's 10/20/70 frame allocates ten parts of transformation attention to algorithms, twenty to technology and data, and seventy to people, organization and process.
This is a heuristic for emphasis. It should not be presented as a measured budget survey or a mandatory spending formula.
Use the large 70% segment to ask who owns skills, incentives, adoption, process controls and new ways of working.
scenes.takeaway: Fund the people-and-process work with the same seriousness as the platform.

scenes.title: The gains are real.|The measures are different.
scenes.description: Controlled studies show meaningful gains in specific settings, not one universal productivity uplift.
notes: The five bars intentionally retain their own outcome definitions. Faster task completion, task speed, completed tasks and issues per hour are not interchangeable measures.

The reported 55.8% faster developer task completion is not treated as a 55.8% time reduction or a universal increase in output. The novice and all-agent support figures come from the same support study, not independent additive gains.
The deck also mentions modeled Anthropic productivity estimates and a P&G team experiment. Those are different evidence types and are not averaged into the controlled-study results.
scenes.takeaway: Use evidence to design your own controlled, workflow-specific evaluation.
scenes.caveat: Different studies, tasks and outcome definitions. Do not average or sum these percentages.

scenes.title: Efficiency is the entry point.|Growth is the next question.
scenes.description: Nordic executives report efficiency far more often than realized revenue growth.

visual.unit: Nordic executive survey / separate, nonexclusive outcomes

notes: Deloitte's Nordic survey of 170 executives reports 79% efficiency benefits, 18% realized revenue growth and 75% expecting revenue impact.
The third ring is explicitly an expectation. These are nonexclusive survey responses and are not parts of a single 100% whole.
The source also reports extensive work redesign at 16%. Its PwC comparison of revenue per employee growth, 27% versus 9% in exposed industries, is an association rather than causal proof.
scenes.takeaway: Ask where AI can change products, services, markets and customer value, not just cost.
scenes.source: Deloitte, State of AI in the Nordics / Apr 2026 / 170 executives
scenes.caveat: Realized benefits and expectations are different measures. Survey responses are nonexclusive.

scenes.title: Give agents a process.|Keep humans in command.
scenes.description: The source projects a growing agentic share of AI value. The operating model must evolve with it.

visual.unit: Agentic share of total AI value / source estimates and forecast

notes: The source's agentic share series is 17% in 2025, 22% in 2026 and a forecast 39% in 2030. The timeline uses real year spacing, not three equally spaced observations.

A separate Gartner forecast says agents may make 15% of daily decisions in 2028 versus 0% in 2024. The Claude API automation share is another distinct measure. Neither is placed on the value-share axis.
A process that delegates execution still needs clear human direction, permissions, review, escalation and rollback.
scenes.takeaway: Design human-directed agent processes, not unbounded automation.
scenes.source: BCG agentic AI value / source slide 12
scenes.caveat: 2030 is a forecast. AI value share is not the share of workers, tasks or decisions automated.

scenes.title: More output.|Not more hours.
scenes.description: Leaders want higher productivity while workers report too little time and energy.

confidence.label: of leaders expect to use digital labor within 12–18 months

notes: The Work Trend Index compares 53% of leaders demanding higher productivity with 80% of workers lacking time or energy to do their work.
The two dot fields represent different respondent groups. The graphic does not subtract the percentages or claim a 27-percentage-point capacity deficit.
82% of leaders express confidence about digital labor within twelve to eighteen months. The deck's 275 interruptions per day statistic applies to the heaviest 20% by ping volume, not all workers.
scenes.takeaway: Create capacity through better work design, not by stretching the working day.
scenes.source: Microsoft Work Trend Index 2025 / 31,000 workers, 31 countries
scenes.caveat: Different respondent groups. Percentages cannot be subtracted to measure a capacity gap.

scenes.title: A different experience|of work is possible.
scenes.description: Frontier leaders and global workers report different experiences. This is an association, not a causal trial.
notes: The five paired comparisons are thriving 39% versus 71%, ability to take on more work 25% versus 55%, meaningful work 77% versus 90%, optimism 80% versus 93%, and fear of AI job loss 43% versus 21%.
Global workers and Frontier leaders are different populations. Their self-reports do not prove that AI caused these differences.
The final row has reversed polarity: a lower fear percentage is favorable. The graphic explicitly marks that direction rather than treating every larger number as better.
scenes.takeaway: Design for agency, meaningful work and capacity, not just tool usage.
scenes.source: Microsoft Work Trend Index / source slide 14
scenes.caveat: Different populations, self-reported outcomes. Final row: lower is better.

scenes.title: The unit of change|is how work gets done.
scenes.description: Three modes can coexist. The leadership move is to design deliberately for each one.
notes: Phase one is a human doing work with an AI assistant. Phase two introduces agents as digital colleagues executing delegated tasks. Phase three has humans directing and governing agent-operated processes.
These modes are not an inevitable linear maturity ladder and do not require every process to become autonomous. All three can coexist in one organization.

The source highlights organization-level factors, 67%, versus individual factors, 32%, as a reminder that operating-model decisions matter. The diagram does not treat those rounded figures as an exhaustive allocation.
scenes.takeaway: Design the work, the decision rights and the controls together.
scenes.caveat: Conceptual operating modes, not measured adoption shares or a mandatory maturity sequence.

scenes.title: The platform is scaling.|The responsibility stays yours.
scenes.description: Six different signals show reach and momentum, not one comparable measure of adoption.

center.label: agents registered
center.detail: Agent 365 registry / Oct 2026. Registered does not mean active.

items.label: active M365 agents / YoY
items.detail: Year-over-year growth in active Microsoft 365 agents.

items.label: GitHub PRs
items.detail: Share of pull requests opened by agents, not merged or accepted.

notes: The source's platform signals are 50 million-plus registered agents, 15-fold annual active M365 agent growth, 30 million-plus paid M365 Copilot seats, 120,000-plus Foundry customers, one in three GitHub pull requests opened by agents, and fivefold daily Copilot user growth.
The registry grew from 40 million in July to more than 50 million in October according to the deck. Registered agents, active agents, seats, customers and pull requests are distinct units.
These numbers are not a basis for saying platform risk is gone. Security, reliability, access controls, observability and business accountability still matter.
scenes.takeaway: Use platform scale as an enabler, not a substitute for governance and evaluation.
scenes.source: Microsoft FY26 Q4 / FY27 Q1 materials; Work Trend Index 2026
scenes.caveat: Source-deck figures. Distinct units; node sizes are decorative, not quantitative. Registration is not active use.

scenes.title: A clear before.|A better after.
scenes.description: Case studies make the ambition concrete. Each result keeps its own baseline and scope.

visual.unit: Each row normalized to its own baseline / lower is better

items.label: Human-handled network tickets
items.detail: Microsoft network operations / approximate after count.

items.label: Support interaction time
items.detail: Source case comparison. Values normalized in seconds: 1,200 to 30.

items.label: Council / tenant reviews
items.detail: Source review-process case; retain this process-specific baseline.

items.label: Daily Azure alerts / Ecolab
items.detail: Baseline is a 30–40 range; after is below 10. Dashed bar is an upper bound of one-third, not an exact result.

notes: The four comparisons show approximately 70,000 to 27,000 human-handled network tickets, twenty minutes to thirty seconds for a support interaction, 133 to forty days for a review process, and thirty to forty daily Azure alerts falling below ten at Ecolab.

Interaction time is normalized using seconds, so thirty seconds is 2.5% of twenty minutes. The Ecolab comparison preserves both its starting range and ending bound; the after bar is less than one-third of the minimum baseline, not a fabricated exact percentage.

These are separate case studies, including an external Ecolab example, not all one Microsoft internal program. The deck also mentions Smart DRI saving around 600 engineering hours monthly, tier-one tickets down 50% and onboarding down 90%.
scenes.takeaway: Choose a 90-day proof with a named baseline, accountable owner and measurable result.
scenes.source: Microsoft Inside Track, 2026 / Ecolab customer story
scenes.caveat: Separate case studies, not controlled causal estimates. Ecolab after-bar is a bound, not an exact observation.

scenes.title: Net job growth.|A very different skills mix.
scenes.description: The World Economic Forum projects substantial job creation and displacement by 2030.

visual.unit: Projected global jobs by 2030 / millions / all macrotrends
visual.skillsLabel: of skills expected to change by 2030

scenes.metricLabel: of skills expected to change by 2030
scenes.insight: Protect the learning pathways that build tomorrow's expertise, including entry-level experience.
notes: The WEF Future of Jobs Report projects 170 million jobs created and 92 million displaced, a net increase of 78 million, by 2030.
This projection covers structural macrotrends, including technology, demographic, economic and green-transition changes. It must not be presented as jobs caused by AI alone.

The source's AI wage premium and early-career employment comparisons are observational associations. They strengthen the case for deliberate reskilling but do not prove a single AI-caused employment effect.
scenes.takeaway: Invest in skills and entry-level learning before the new operating model needs them.
scenes.caveat: 2030 projection across all macrotrends, not an AI-only job forecast.

scenes.title: Build the foundations.|Then compound the value.
scenes.description: Data, identity and governance turn promising experiments into systems the business can trust.

readiness.label: Nordic firms fully EU AI Act ready

risks.label: AI projects at risk without AI-ready data
risks.detail: Gartner forecast of abandonment through 2026, conditional on lack of AI-ready data.

risks.label: agentic projects forecast canceled by end-2027
risks.detail: Gartner forecast, June 2025. Different scope and denominator from the data-readiness forecast.

notes: The source presents five different signals: a forecast that 60% of projects without AI-ready data are abandoned through 2026; a forecast that more than 40% of agentic projects are canceled by end-2027; 43% strategic preparedness among Nordic firms; 5% with full agent controls; and 3% fully ready for the EU AI Act in a Nordic survey.
These are distinct populations, dates and definitions. The visual separates reported readiness from forecast risk rather than pretending they form a single funnel or probability model.

The source mentions a December 2027 legal timetable based on a July 2026 legal update. That claim has not been independently verified and is not reproduced as compliance guidance. Confirm applicable requirements and current law with qualified counsel.
scenes.takeaway: Put AI-ready data and agent governance before broad scaling.
scenes.source: Gartner 2025 / Deloitte, BCG and Tieto 2026 / source slide 18
scenes.caveat: Separate studies and forecasts, not a combined risk score. Verify current legal requirements independently.

scenes.title: Twenty-five minutes.|Three commitments.
scenes.description: A suggested executive conversation. Select an act below to rehearse its opening scene.

asks.label: Name three workflows
asks.detail: P&L-relevant outcomes to redesign with agents.

asks.label: Fund the 70%
asks.detail: People, process and organization, not just technology.

asks.label: Build before scaling
asks.detail: AI-ready data and agent governance first.

notes: This is the source's suggested twenty-five-minute executive arc: three minutes for the hook, four for urgency, five for tension, five for the reframe, five for vision and three for the call to action.
The six time segments use proportional lengths. Selecting a rehearsal card jumps to the opening scene of that segment; this is not an autoplay timer.
Close with three decisions: name three P&L workflows, fund the people-and-process work, and establish data readiness and agent governance before scaling.
scenes.takeaway: Leave the room with commitments, not just enthusiasm.

scenes.title: The next move|is yours.
scenes.description: Usage is everywhere. Value is not. Redesign the work that matters.

items.label: Workflows
items.detail: Name the outcomes. Assign the owners.

visual.closing: Start with one measurable outcome. Build for the organization you want to become.

notes: The source closes with 'The question is no longer whether. It is how fast.' Use that urgency with judgment: the real decision is where to create measurable value responsibly.
Bring the conversation back to the three commitments: redesign three workflows, fund the organizational change and put trustworthy foundations in place.
The visual numbers are commitments and the source's heuristic, not three new research statistics. The single foundation means an integrated capability, not one product.
scenes.takeaway: Turn the AI conversation into a small number of accountable leadership decisions.

scenes.title: The evidence|behind the argument.
scenes.description: Business value, adoption, economics and readiness. Original links supplied in the source deck.
notes: These are the first fifteen source-deck references. They are preserved as supplied; URLs, dates and claims have not been independently reverified.
The deck mixes forecasts, survey findings, observational comparisons and controlled studies. Those distinctions are retained in each relevant scene.
scenes.takeaway: Check the original definition, population and publication date before reusing a claim.

scenes.title: The research|behind the work.
scenes.description: Jobs, productivity, Frontier Firms and case studies. Links retained from the supplied presentation.
notes: These are the remaining fifteen references from the source deck, including productivity studies, labor-market research, Work Trend Index material and operational case studies.
The legal update is retained for source traceability, not endorsed as current compliance advice. Verify current law and applicability independently.
scenes.takeaway: Keep forecasts, case studies and causal evidence in their own lanes.
